correctness.rationale: Exactly 19,355 labeled simple cubic graphs are generated by a unique residual-degree recursion, of which 19,320 are connected, comprising five classes. Independently constructed matrices and unit-filtration computations agree on all 5 determinants and Smith lists.

value.rationale: The full five-isomorphism-class order-eight cubic family is a canonical small complete classification, not an ad hoc parameter cut. All five associated symmetric-exclusion graphs have the same 28/72 and 12×4 plus 16×6 degree data, but distinct integral sandpile groups. In particular cube and Wagner token graphs differ sharply in odd-prime torsion. The complete group decompositions are not recoverable merely from counting the token configurations or spanning trees and provide a natural exact integral benchmark for chip-firing in two-particle configuration networks; no larger-order theorem is claimed.
